questions.text: Which of the following function is not performed by Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: To accept deposits on interest from public

questions.explanation:
The incorrect statement is To accept deposits on interest from the public.

Key PointsReserve Bank of India -The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was founded in 1935 as a private organisation before becoming India's central bank in 1949.

The RBI's primary objective is to carry out comprehensive supervision of the Indian financial sector, which consists of commercial banks, financial institutions, and non-banking financing companies.

Important PointsFunctions of Reserve Bank of India are as follows - 

1. Monetary Authority - The RBI's primary responsibility is developing and implementing India's monetary policy. The RBI's major problem as a monetary authority is striking a balance between "price stability" and "future economic growth."

2. Currency Issuer - The RBI is in charge of printing and releasing fresh banknotes in India.

3. Regulator and supervisor of the financial system - RBI establishes the guidelines by which Indian banks and the financial system must function.

4. Government banker - The RBI is the retail bank for the Government of India, much as retail and commercial banks provide services to the general public (GOI). For the GOI, RBI also serves as a merchant banker.

5. Foreign Exchange's Manager - In India, all money transfers must follow FEMA regulations (Foreign Exchange Management Act). The RBI is in charge of making sure that transactions follow FEMA regulations.

6. Banker to Banks - The RBI has an account with every bank in India. In this account, they maintain their required reserves and other deposits. Therefore, RBI also serves as a bank to the banks in this way. The RBI is in charge of overseeing interbank transactions. As a rare circumstance, RBI may also extend credit to banks.

Thus, To accept deposits on interest from public is not a function performed by Reserve Bank of India. It is a function of Commercial Banks.

questions.text: How many sub-indices are there in the Financial Inclusion Index report released by RBI?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 3.

Key Points

  • There are 3 sub-indices in the Financial Inclusion Index Report released by the RBI.
  • The sub Indices are further divided into the following:
    • Access-  Divided into four dimensions. Banking, Digital, Pension and Insurance. Comprised of 26  Indicators.
    • Usage-  Divided into five dimensions. Savings and Investment, Credit, Digital, Insurance and  Pension. Comprised of 52 Indicators.
    • Quality- Divided into three dimensions. Financial Literacy, Consumer protection, and inequality. With a total of 19 indicators.

questions.text: In January 2024, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the minimum capital requirement for Small Finance Banks (SFBs) from Rs 100 crore to Rs __________ Payments Banks to upgrade as SFBs.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 200 crore.

In News

  • RBI doubles the minimum capital requirement to Rs 200 cr for SFB.

Key Points

  • The Reserve Bank raised the minimum capital requirement for small finance banks to Rs 200 crore and permitted Payments Bank to upgrade as SFBs. 
  • This move aims to enhance the financial resilience of SFBs and ensure their long-term sustainability.
  • It is worth noting that all SFBs currently in operation have a net worth exceeding Rs 200 crore.
  • For Primary urban cooperative banks that voluntarily wish to transition into SFBs, the initial net worth requirement has been set at Rs 100 crore.
  • These UCBs must increase their net worth to Rs 200 crore within five years from the commencement of business.
  • Payments banks, after five years of operations and meeting the eligibility criteria, can apply for conversion into SFBs.
  • This provision opens up new opportunities for payment banks to expand their services and cater to a broader customer base.

Additional Information

  • RBI
    • Established in - 1935
    • HQ - Mumbai
    • Governor - ShaktiKanta Das
  • Note: In May 2024 RBI has updated the minimum capital requirement for small finance bank upto 300cr.

questions.text: According to section ________ of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the bank has full authority to issue banknotes of all denominations.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 22.Key Points

  • According to Section 22 of the RBI Act, 1934 the Reserve bank of India has sole right to issue currency or print currency in India.
  • Section 25 of the RBI Act, 1934 provides that the design, form, and material of bank notes shall be such as may be approved by the Central Government after consideration of the recommendations made by the Central Board of RBI.
  • Section 24 of the RBI Act 1934 states that the maximum denomination of note printed in India is Rs.10000.
  • Section 26 of the RBI Act 1934 states the legal tender character of Indian banknotes.

Additional Information

  • RBI was established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act,1934.
  • Current Governor of RBI is Sanjay Malhotra(26th).
  • Sir Osborne Smith was the first governor of RBI and C.D Deshmukh was the first Indian governor of RBI.
  • It operates the currency and credit system of the country.
  • It is called the Bankers Bank of India.
  • It formulates, implements, and monitors the monetary policy.

questions.text: As per the Reserve Bank of India, what is the target and tolerance band for inflation?

options.text: the target of 4.5 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band
the target of 2.5 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band
the target of 3.5 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band
the target of 4 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band
the target of 5.5 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is the target of 4 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band.

Key Points

  • The Reserve Bank of India proposed to retain the current numerical framework for the target and tolerance band for inflation — the target of 4 percent with a plus or minus two percent tolerance band — for the next five years.
  • This has been proposed due to the repetitive incidence of supply shocks, still elevated inflation expectations, and projection errors.
  • The RBI said, 'The current tolerance band of plus or minus two percent may be retained notwithstanding the central tendency emerging from the country's experience of lowering targets and narrowing bands over time.

questions.text: As per the RBI's guidelines on Responsible Lending Conduct, the Regulated Entities (REs) shall release all the original movable/immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of _______ days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan account.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 30.

Key Points

  • As per the RBI's guidelines on Responsible Lending Conduct, the Regulated Entities (REs) shall release all the original movable/immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan account.
    • The borrower shall be given the option of collecting the original movable/immovable property documents either from the banking outlet/branch where the loan account was serviced or any other office of the RE where the documents are available, as per her / his preference.
    • In case of delay in releasing of original movable/immovable property documents or failure to file charge satisfaction form with the relevant registry beyond 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan, the RE shall communicate to the borrower the reasons for such delay.
    • In the case where the delay is attributable to the RE, it shall compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000/- for each day of delay.

questions.text: The Reserve Bank of India has granted a Payment Aggregator license to Mumbai-based Mswipe Technologies Private Limited. It is issued under which section of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Section 7.

In News

  • RBI grants payment aggregator license to Mswipe Technologies.

Key Points

  • Merchant-led digital payments provider Mswipe Technologies said the Reserve Bank of India had granted it a payment aggregator (PA) license.
  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) granted a Payment Aggregator (PA) license to Mswipe Technologies Private Limited under Section 7 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
  • The company received an in-principle nod from the central bank to operate as a payment aggregator in August 2022.
  • After receiving RBI’s in-principle nod for the license, Mswipe was looking to pilot its payment gateway stack with its existing merchant base.
  • It also aids offline merchants with loans as well as store and inventory management solutions.

Additional Information

  • RBI
    • ​Established in - 1935
    • HQ - Mumbai
    • Governor - ShaktiKanta Das
  • ​Mswipe Technologies Private Limited
    • Founded in - 2011
    • It provides payment solutions, including point-of-sale devices, unified payments interface (UPI), quick response codes and payment links to help offline merchants receive payments digitally.
    • HQ - Mumbai

questions.text: In February 2024, RBI allows banks, and non-banks to issue PPIs to commuters for Public Transport. What is the Cash loading limit of PPIs?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Rs 50,000/- per month.

In News

  • RBI allows banks, and non-banks to issue PPIs to commuters for public transport.

Key Points

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) amended the Master Direction on prepaid payment instruments (PPI), allowing banks and non-bank PPI issuers to give these instruments for public transport. 
  • The cash loading of PPIs is limited to ₹50,000/- per month subject to the overall limit of the PPI (not permitted in one type of Small PPI).
  • The limit on loading of PPIs via electronic/online means is subject to the overall limit of the PPI.
  • In an announcement, the RBI said, "To provide convenience, speed, affordability, and safety of digital modes of payment to commuters for transit services, it has been decided to permit authorized bank and non-bank PPI issuers to issue PPIs for making payments across various public transport systems."
  • The Master Directions on PPIs were originally issued in 2021.
  • The total amount debited during any given month shall not exceed ₹10,000/-.

Additional Information

  • PPIs
    • PPIs are instruments that facilitate the purchase of goods and services, conduct of financial services, enable remittance facilities, etc., against the value stored therein.
  • RBI
    • ​Established in - 1935
    • HQ - Mumbai
    • Governor - ShaktiKanta Das

questions.text:
Consider the statements: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. RBI launches the March 2024 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households.

B. The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments of price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, across 20 cities.

C. The agency, M/s Hansa Research Group Pvt. Ltd. Mumbai has been engaged to conduct the survey of this round on behalf of the RBI.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Both A and C.

In News

  • The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting a Consumer Confidence Survey (CCS). The March 2024 round of the survey is being launched.

Key Points

  • RBI launches the March 2024 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households.
  • The survey seeks qualitative responses from households, regarding their sentiments on the general economic situation, employment scenario, price level, household income, and spending.
  • The survey is conducted regularly in 19 cities, viz., Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram. 
  • The agency, M/s Hansa Research Group Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai has been engaged to conduct the survey of this round on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India.
  • For this purpose, the selected households will be approached by the agency and they are requested to provide their responses.
  • Other individuals, who are not approached by the agency, can also participate in this survey by providing their responses using the linked survey schedule. 

Additional Information

  • RBI 
    • ​Established in 1935
    • HQ - Mumbai
    • Governor - ShaktiKanta Das

questions.text: The RBI has announced the formation of a 10-member 'Expert Committee on Benchmarking of its Statistics'. Who is heading this committee?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Michael Debabrata Patra.

In News

  • The RBI has announced setting up a 10-member ‘Expert Committee on Benchmarking of its Statistics’ under the leadership of deputy governor Michael Debabrata Patra.

Key Points

  • Michael Debabrata Patra is the deputy governor of the RBI and is heading this committee.
  • The committee has been tasked to submit its report by the end of November 2024.
  • It will also study the quality of other regular data and provide guidance on further data refinement.
  • Members include RBI executive directors Muneesh Kapur and O P Mall, and experts such as R B Barman and Sonalde Desai.

Additional Information

  • Michael Debabrata Patra
    • He is the deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
    • Patra has extensive experience in economic research and monetary policy formulation.
    • He has served as the executive director of the Monetary Policy Department of RBI before being appointed as deputy governor.
    • He has also represented India at various international forums and has a deep understanding of macroeconomic issues.
  • RBI's Expert Committee on Benchmarking Statistics
    • The committee is formed to benchmark the quality of the RBI’s statistics against global standards.
    • It includes members from various prestigious institutions and former officials with significant experience in statistics and data management.
    • The committee's mandate includes evaluating the current statistical processes and suggesting improvements.
    • The final report will guide the RBI in refining its data collection and analysis methods, which are crucial for policy formulation.
